transcript.content: Good [morning/afternoon], welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, I suppose I’m here because I’m tired of working my days around what I’m trying not to run into. I’ve got a workshop at home—used to spend a lot of time out there, fixing little things, making shelves and whatnot—but lately I just steer clear of it. And family gatherings, too, if there’s a chance my brother-in-law might be there.

It’s gotten old, you know? After all this time, still planning around reminders like that. I don’t want to keep doing that.
When you avoid your workshop or family gatherings, is it because you’re worried something bad might happen—like panic, anxiety, or losing control?

It’s not exactly that I think something bad is going to happen, like I’ll lose control. It’s more… I just don’t want to be around the reminders. The workshop used to be my place, you know, tools laid out just so—my father kept his like that too, though he’d yell if you moved a wrench half an inch.

But anyway, I catch myself avoiding it now. Same with family things if my brother-in-law might be there. I just steer away from all of it, and I’m tired of arranging my life around what I might run into.
When you think about the workshop or being around your brother-in-law, does it bring up specific memories or feelings that are hard to deal with?

Yes… yes, it does. Not always when I expect it, though. That’s the odd part.

I can be doing something completely ordinary, like shaving in the morning, or working on a painting—I took that up more after I stopped doing as much in the workshop, though I’m not especially good, mostly landscapes—and then out of nowhere I’ll see his hand again. Holding that heavy tool. Just like a picture that pops into my head.

And when it does, my chest tightens up. It’s not something I go looking for. It just shows up.
Do you find yourself feeling angry, guilty, or emotionally numb in relation to these memories or reminders?

Guilty, mostly. Angry too, I suppose, but the guilt is what sticks.

I keep going back over it in my head, telling myself I should’ve put my foot down sooner… never let him stay with us in the first place. I know people say you can’t know how things will turn out, but still, I think maybe if I’d handled it more like a man, none of this would’ve happened.

It’s silly, maybe. My wife used to say I could turn a grocery list into a courtroom argument, and I do that with myself now. Just keep trying the case over and over.
